correctness.rationale: By homogeneity, two injective ordered tuples are in the same automorphism orbit exactly when their coordinate-labelled induced finite substructures agree. Choosing which \(p\) coordinates lie on the left contributes \(\binom np\), the two internal structures contribute \(f_p g_{n-p}\), and the unrestricted bipartite cross relation contributes \(2^{p(n-p)}\). Every finite structure embeds in the Fraïssé limit, so the count is exact. For pure finite sets and finite linear orders, \(f_p=1\) and \(g_q=q!\), yielding the displayed closed form; formal rearrangement gives both OEIS exponential generating functions. Partitioning an arbitrary ordered tuple by its equality kernel gives the Stirling transform. A fresh computation reproduced \(1,2,7,43,441,7241,185233,7252337,429318529,38079107713,5026601726721\), matching OEIS A340335, and the actual frozen verifier was read.
correctness.risk: The transform is elementary once the mixed-sum definition and homogeneity are in place; its contribution is the general orbit-profile formula and identification.

value.rationale: Orbit profiles are a canonical quantitative invariant of oligomorphic homogeneous structures. The theorem gives a reusable transform for an entire natural Fraïssé construction and identifies the precise profile of the torsion-free Kubiś-Shelah example with a pre-existing OEIS sequence. Although the derivation is short, the object and invariant are independently motivated and the formula packages exact information that is useful across mixed-sum examples.
value.risk: The mathematics is elementary once the correct invariant is posed, so its value is as an exact general transform and identification rather than a deep structural theorem.

final_claim: For mixed sums of relational Fraïssé classes with strong amalgamation and finite labeled age profiles \(f_p,g_p\), the injective ordered \(n\)-tuple orbit count of the Fraïssé limit is \(a_n=\sum_{p=0}^n\binom np f_p g_{n-p}2^{p(n-p)}\); all ordered-tuple orbits are the Stirling transform \(b_n=\sum_k S(n,k)a_k\). For the Kubiś-Shelah finite-set/linear-order mixed sum this gives \(a_n=n!\sum_{p=0}^n2^{p(n-p)}/p!\), exactly OEIS A340335, with the stated two equivalent exponential generating functions.
limitations: Requires finite labeled age profiles in each arity.
The OEIS sequence and generating functions themselves are prior work; novelty is restricted to the general transform and model-theoretic identification.
